findings.desc: CHK-008:edge:1 is marked covered by packages/main/src/tasks/unattended-dispatch-smoke.ts, but that smoke only asserts cancellation, accepted review, missing policy, unavailable/unattendedUnsafe host, and authority invariants (see lines 271-459). It does not exercise the required timeout, missing-receipt, or mixed-worker-outcome paths. Those scenarios only appear in dispatch-run-smoke under CHK-007 (e.g. missing transcript/receipt at 1777-1830 and mixed worker outcomes at 1833-1853), so the recorded evidence/test-evidence overclaims final CHK-008 edge coverage.

dispatch_auto authorizes on env and runtime policy fields that the fake unattended runner never enforces. checkDispatchPolicy requires env and runtime metadata (packages/main/src/core/dispatch-policy.ts:385-409), but runRequiredCommands executes child commands with execSync using the parent process environment and no timeout or env override (packages/main/src/core/lattice-dispatch.ts:1330-1343). Verified in an isolated temp repo: policy envAllowlist=[] and envDenylist=[REVIEW_LANE_SECRET], then dispatch_auto with a fake requiredCommand that writes process.env.REVIEW_LANE_SECRET still returned status=accepted_local and produced leakedValue=lane-secret-value. That means unattended jobs can read caller secrets despite an explicit denylist, and maxRuntimeMinutes is likewise not enforced on the execution path.

dispatch_auto does not enforce policy scope or command allowlists before execution. buildPack copies caller-supplied allowedPaths and requiredCommands directly into the pack (packages/main/src/core/lattice-dispatch.ts:945-969), dispatchAuto only checks host and maxParallel before forwarding the original args into runDispatch (2203-2273), and the fake runner executes pack.requiredCommands verbatim (1544-1556). Verified in an isolated temp repo using built dist handlers: a policy with allowedPaths=[packages/main/src/generated/] and commandAllowlist=[node -e process.exit(0)] still accepted dispatch_auto with allowedPaths=[README.md] and requiredCommands=[node -e require(fs).writeFileSync(UNSAFE-CMD.txt,x)], returned status=accepted_local, and created the file. This breaks the user-approved host/path/command boundary promised by the story.
